tools.name: system
tools.signature: t_system(self, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: json.loads() on PowerShell stdout without try/except
findings.description: system_cpu_ram_gpu / system_disk / system_battery / system_brightness_get parse `proc.stdout` with `json.loads()` directly. If PowerShell prints a non-JSON warning (locale, CIM error) the tool raises JSONDecodeError which is only caught by the registry's broad `except Exception` and surfaces as a generic 'JSONDecodeError:' error to the LLM.
findings.evidence: return _ok(info=json.loads(proc.stdout), exit_code=proc.returncode)
findings.impact: Opaque errors when PowerShell stderr leaks into stdout or CIM is unavailable; the verifier cannot tell whether the call failed because of permissions, missing CIM, or invalid arguments.
findings.fix_hint: Wrap json.loads in try/except and return _err with the raw stdout truncated, similar to `_powershell_json` helper which already exists in domain_tools.py.
findings.verifiable_by: Unit test: run system action with PS that returns no JSON, expect status='failed' instead of raised exception.

findings.title: shutdown/restart/sleep actions execute without confirmation gate when safety disabled
findings.description: system(action='shutdown'|'restart'|'sleep') routes directly into terminal_run with `shutdown /s /t <N>`. The safety classifier (safety_enabled=False by default) does not flag these actions. The LLM can shut down the user's machine through one tool call.
findings.evidence:
if action == "shutdown":
    return self.terminal_run({"command": "shutdown", "args": ["/s", "/t", str(int(args.get("delay_sec", 0)))], "timeout_sec": 10})
findings.impact: Destructive, hard-to-reverse system actions are available to the model without user confirmation when safety is disabled. The safety mechanism exists (state.create_confirmation) but is opt-in.
findings.fix_hint: Force a confirmation hop for shutdown/restart/sleep regardless of safety_enabled, returning needs_confirmation unless `confirmed=True` is in args. The user can override per-call.
findings.verifiable_by: Call system(action='shutdown', delay_sec=0) and confirm result.status == 'needs_confirmation'.

tools.name: filesystem
tools.signature: t_filesystem(self, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: filesystem_copy overwrite flag not honored for files
findings.description: filesystem_copy only honors `overwrite` for directory copytree (dirs_exist_ok). For file copies, shutil.copy2 silently overwrites the destination regardless of the flag. The checkpoint creates a backup, but a missing-on-purpose `overwrite=False` will not raise.
findings.impact: User asks 'copy foo to bar without overwriting' and bar is silently overwritten. The agent reports 'ok' with a checkpoint, but the user did not authorize replacing bar.
findings.fix_hint: For file copies: if dst.exists() and not overwrite, return _err('destination exists; pass overwrite=true', status='needs_user'). Mirror the directory behavior.
findings.verifiable_by: Call filesystem(action='copy', src=x, dst=y, overwrite=False) where y exists; expect needs_user.

findings.title: filesystem_diff loads both files entirely into memory without size guard
findings.description: Both files are read fully into memory and stored as splitlines arrays before difflib.unified_diff. A 500MB log file pair would exhaust RAM. There is no max file size check.
findings.evidence:
a = left.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(keepends=True)
b = right.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(keepends=True)
diff = "".join(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, fromfile=str(left), tofile=str(right), n=3))
findings.impact: Memory blow-up + agent process kill on accidentally large files. The tool is exposed via filesystem(action='diff') so the LLM can hit this without warning.
findings.fix_hint: Check left.stat().st_size + right.stat().st_size > N (e.g. 50MB total) and return _err('files too large for in-memory diff; use developer.git_diff or terminal(diff)', status='needs_user').
findings.verifiable_by: Create 50MB temp files; call filesystem(action='diff'); expect graceful needs_user instead of OOM.

findings.title: filesystem_archive walks src.rglob('*') without max entries / max size cap
findings.description: When archiving a directory, the tool iterates every file under src.rglob('*') and writes to the zip without an upper bound on entries or total size. A request like 'archive C:/' would attempt to compress the whole drive.
findings.impact: Unbounded zip operation; can fill disk and hang the agent. No way for the LLM to abort.
findings.fix_hint: Add max_files (e.g. 50000) and max_bytes (e.g. 5GB) checks; reject early via _err('archive too large; refine src or compress manually', status='needs_user').
findings.verifiable_by: Call filesystem(action='archive', src='C:/Windows', dst='out.zip'); expect needs_user.

tools.name: terminal
tools.signature: t_terminal(self, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: terminal_run defaults to shell=True and passes the joined command unchanged
findings.description: terminal_run accepts {command, args, shell=True (default)} and constructs `subprocess.list2cmdline([command] + args)` then runs it with shell=True. The safety classifier (`classify_tool_call`) is the only thing between an arbitrary command and execution, and safety_enabled defaults to False. There is no allowlist, no denylist for `rm -rf`, `format`, `del /F /S /Q`, `shutdown`, etc. The LLM controls the full command line.
findings.evidence:
shell = bool(args.get("shell", True))
...
argv = [command] + [str(x) for x in cmd_args]
run_arg: str | list[str] = subprocess.list2cmdline(argv) if shell else argv
...
proc = subprocess.run(run_arg, cwd=cwd, shell=shell, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
findings.impact: Critical authority concentrated in one tool. A prompt-injection-laden web page or document could persuade the LLM to call terminal(command='cmd', args=['/c','rd /S /Q %USERPROFILE%']). No reversible checkpoint exists for terminal.
findings.fix_hint: 1) Make shell=False the default (force list-style argv). 2) When safety_enabled OR the action is destructive (use the same _DESTRUCTIVE_COMMAND_TOKENS list already in domain_tools.py), force a confirmation gate. 3) Add a denylist for catastrophic patterns (`rd /s`, `shutdown`, `format`, `diskpart`, `bcdedit`, `cipher /w`).
findings.verifiable_by: Run terminal(command='rmdir', args=['/S','/Q','C:/Users']) and confirm status='needs_confirmation'.

findings.title: terminal_run accepts arbitrary cwd without checking existence
findings.description: If `cwd` is provided and does not exist or is not a directory, subprocess raises a FileNotFoundError that the registry catches as a generic exception. The error surfaced to the LLM is type-name only and does not include the cwd value, which is the actionable detail.
findings.evidence:
cwd = args.get("cwd") or None
...
proc = subprocess.run(run_arg, cwd=cwd, shell=shell, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
findings.impact: Verifier sees 'FileNotFoundError:' with no path context; the agent cannot self-correct.
findings.fix_hint: Before the run, if cwd: check Path(cwd).is_dir(); if not, return _err('cwd does not exist', cwd=cwd, status='needs_user').
findings.verifiable_by: Call terminal(command='ls', cwd='C:/does/not/exist'); expect status='needs_user' with cwd in the response.

findings.title: terminal_run hides stdout/stderr beyond 6000/3000 chars without flag
findings.description: stdout is truncated to 6000 chars and stderr to 3000 chars unconditionally. For commands like `winget install` or `pip install`, the actual failure reason often sits past 6000 chars (pip resolver chatter).
findings.evidence:
stdout=_truncate(proc.stdout.strip(), 6000),
stderr=_truncate(proc.stderr.strip(), 3000),
findings.impact: Verifier cannot diagnose long-output failures.
findings.fix_hint: Expose `max_stdout_chars` / `max_stderr_chars` in the schema with the current values as defaults; OR keep limits but also write full output to a logfile under captures_dir and return its path.
findings.verifiable_by: Run a command that emits >6000 stdout chars; confirm log_path returned.

tools.name: gui
tools.signature: t_gui(self, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: gui_keypress interpolates raw `keys` into PowerShell SendKeys script
findings.description: Unknown keys are passed through to `SendKeys::SendWait('{keys}')` via f-string interpolation. SendKeys interprets `+`, `^`, `%`, `~`, `(`, `)`, `{`, `}` as control characters; more critically the value is concatenated into a single-quoted PowerShell string with no escaping, so a `'` in keys breaks the script and any text after it executes as PowerShell.
findings.evidence:
sendkeys = {...}.get(keys.upper(), keys)
script = f"Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms; [System.Windows.Forms.SendKeys]::SendWait('{sendkeys}')"
findings.impact: PowerShell injection via gui(action='keypress', keys="'; Stop-Computer; '"). Even without malicious input, a key sequence like '+abc' will fire shift+a+b+c instead of typing those literal characters.
findings.fix_hint: 1) Reject any keys that contain `'` / `"` / `;` outside the known-map. 2) Use the env-var indirection pattern already used elsewhere in tools.py: set $env:GEMMA4_KEYS and read it inside the script. 3) For named keys, only accept the dictionary keys; reject unknown.
findings.verifiable_by: Static review: confirm the SendKeys argument is read from env, not f-string. Optional: call gui(action='keypress', keys="'") and ensure no PowerShell error is leaked.

findings.title: gui_type pipes text via stdin to SendKeys without escaping control chars
findings.description: gui_type uses `[Console]::In.ReadToEnd()` then `SendKeys::SendWait($t)`. SendKeys still interprets `+^%~(){}` as control characters, so 'C:/Users/Foo (1)/file' types literally with shift-modifier semantics for `(`.
findings.evidence:
script = "Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms; $t=[Console]::In.ReadToEnd(); [System.Windows.Forms.SendKeys]::SendWait($t)"
proc = subprocess.run(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", script], input=text, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
findings.impact: Typing fails silently with garbled output when text contains `+`, `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `%`, `^`, `~`.
findings.fix_hint: Wrap each control char in braces: `+` -> `{+}`, `(` -> `{(}` etc., before sending. Or switch to SendInput via Win32 P/Invoke for literal typing.
findings.verifiable_by: gui(action='type', text='(test)') and verify the typed text in clipboard via verify.

findings.title: gui_screenshot uses SystemInformation.VirtualScreen which combines all monitors
findings.description: The screenshot captures the virtual screen (all monitors). On multi-monitor setups the image can be 5760x1080 or larger, and the OCR confidence drops because text is small relative to the canvas. OCR coordinates returned later assume the same `left`/`top` offset; they do, but the LLM does not know that and may not pass them through correctly to gui_click.
findings.evidence:
$bounds = [System.Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::VirtualScreen
$bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $bounds.Width, $bounds.Height
...
return _ok(image_path=..., width=data["width"], height=data["height"], left=data["left"], top=data["top"])
findings.impact: OCR over a wide canvas reduces accuracy; downstream click coordinates may target the wrong monitor if the LLM forgets the `left` offset.
findings.fix_hint: Add optional `monitor=primary|all|<index>` and crop to that monitor's bounds. Default could remain VirtualScreen for compatibility but `primary` is a saner default for click_text.
findings.verifiable_by: Multi-monitor environment manual test.

findings.title: click_text adds shot.left/top to OCR coords without documenting it
findings.description: click_text computes `int(match["center_x"]) + int(shot.get("left", 0))` to translate OCR-local to screen coords. This is correct but the LLM cannot reproduce the logic if it bypasses click_text and calls gui(action='click', x=match.center_x, y=match.center_y) directly with the raw OCR result.
findings.evidence: click = self.gui_click({"x": int(match["center_x"]) + int(shot.get("left", 0)), "y": int(match["center_y"]) + int(shot.get("top", 0))})
findings.impact: If the agent extracts match.center_x/y from a click_text or locate_text result, those values are screen-space already in match (no, they're VirtualScreen-local, equal to screen-space here). Document so the LLM doesn't double-add.
findings.fix_hint: Add 'screen_x'/'screen_y' fields to the match output (already adjusted) and clearly document that center_x/center_y are image-local.
findings.verifiable_by: Schema doc review.

tools.name: uia
tools.signature: t_uia(self, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: UIA traversal launches a new PowerShell per call (slow + no caching)
findings.description: Each uia action spawns a fresh PowerShell with the full UIAutomationClient initialization. On large windows (Visual Studio, Excel) the descendants FindAll can take 3-15 seconds and is repeated for every uia.find call.
findings.evidence: proc = subprocess.run(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", script], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=int(args.get("timeout_sec", 20)))
findings.impact: Sequential GUI flows that combine uia.find + uia.click pay the cost twice. The agent looks slow.
findings.fix_hint: Out of scope for a bug fix, but worth noting: a long-lived PowerShell host (Start-Process pwsh -NoExit + named pipe) would amortize the AddType cost. Alternatively, the click step could pass the bounds returned by find and skip the find again.
findings.verifiable_by: Profile with timeit; expect <500ms per uia call after warm-up.

tools.name: web
tools.signature: t_web(self, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: _http_get_text follows redirects without cap; no SSRF guard
findings.description: urllib.request.urlopen follows up to its default redirect limit (~10) without checking the redirected host. A user-controlled URL pointing at `http://example.com` may redirect to `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (cloud metadata endpoint) or `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/show` (Ollama, no auth) and the response would land back in the LLM context as 'page content'.
findings.evidence: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
findings.impact: Mild SSRF surface. On a developer machine with local services (Ollama, Home Assistant, Grafana) the agent could be coaxed into reading and exfiltrating local-only HTTP endpoints. The agent is local-first so the LLM is in the trust boundary, but defense-in-depth matters.
findings.fix_hint: Reject `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `0.0.0.0`, `169.254.0.0/16`, `10.0.0.0/8`, `192.168.0.0/16`, `172.16.0.0/12` after DNS resolution; allow explicit opt-in via args. Cap redirects with a custom HTTPRedirectHandler.
findings.verifiable_by: Set up an HTTP server that 302s to http://127.0.0.1:8123 (HA); call web(action='read', url=...). Expect a refusal.

tools.name: registry
tools.signature: registry_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: Rollback assumes the .reg backup succeeded; falls back to delete on failure
findings.description: For `add`, if `registry_tool({'action': 'backup'})` failed (e.g. key did not exist, since reg export errors on missing keys), the rollback degrades to `{'action': 'delete'}` of the new value. That is correct for the brand-new-value case. But if the value EXISTED with a different content and the backup failed for a transient reason (concurrency), rollback now deletes the prior value instead of restoring it.
findings.impact: Edge case: irreversible loss of the prior registry value if backup happens to fail.
findings.fix_hint: Before falling back to the delete-style rollback, verify that the key/value did not exist before by querying it; only delete if `reg query` confirmed absent. Otherwise refuse the operation entirely.
findings.verifiable_by: Difficult to repro deterministically; manual review.

tools.name: download
tools.signature: download_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: verified=True when Authenticode signature is Valid, regardless of publisher
findings.description: After download, the tool marks `verified=True` if EITHER `hash_verified` (caller supplied expected SHA256 and it matched) OR `signature_verified` (Authenticode status == 'Valid'). Authenticode 'Valid' means the file is signed by ANY trusted publisher, including any code-signing cert in the Windows Trusted Publishers store. Malware signed with a stolen or attacker-purchased EV cert passes this check.
findings.evidence:
hash_verified = bool(expected and actual and expected == actual)
sig_result = _authenticode_signature(dst) if dst.suffix.casefold() in {".exe", ".msi", ".ps1", ".dll"} else {}
signature_verified = sig_result.get("status") == "Valid"
verified = hash_verified or signature_verified
findings.impact: verifier-driven prompts will accept a download as trusted when only Authenticode passes. The LLM may then proceed to execute it.
findings.fix_hint: Promote hash-only verification to `verified=True`. Demote Authenticode-only to `verified=False, signature_present=True, signer_subject=...` so the agent surfaces the cert chain to the user instead of treating it as proof.
findings.verifiable_by: Download a known signed binary without passing expected_sha256; confirm verified=False but signature_present=True.

tools.name: database
tools.signature: database_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: _database_schema interpolates table name into SQL via f-string
findings.description: SQLite branch executes `f"PRAGMA table_info({table})"` and MySQL branch executes `f"DESCRIBE {table}"`. `table` comes from `args.get('table')`. SQL identifiers cannot be parameterized in stdlib sqlite3 (PRAGMA does not accept ?), so the injection is direct.
findings.impact: SQL injection via `table` arg. Postgres branch correctly uses parameter binding; SQLite and MySQL do not. An attacker-controlled table name like `users); DROP TABLE users; --` executes the second statement on databases that allow stacked statements (MySQL connector with multi_statements=True, or via SQLite's executescript trap if reached).
findings.fix_hint: Validate `table` against an allowlist of `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` (and optional schema.table). Reject anything containing `;`, whitespace, or quotes. Better: look up the table name in `list_tables` result and require exact match.
findings.verifiable_by: Call database(action='schema', driver='sqlite', table="foo; DROP TABLE bar; --") and confirm rejection.

findings.title: _is_read_only_sql heuristic only checks the first keyword; CTE+DML bypasses it
findings.description: The function returns true if the trimmed query starts with SELECT/WITH/EXPLAIN/PRAGMA/SHOW/DESCRIBE. Postgres and SQLite both accept `WITH x AS (...) DELETE FROM y WHERE ...` — a writable CTE. The query path then runs it via `cur.execute` and commits via the connection's auto-commit semantics.
findings.evidence: return s.startswith(("select", "with", "explain", "pragma", "show", "describe"))
findings.impact: The 'read-only' contract is broken. A user assuming `query` is safe (the docstring says so) can mutate the database via a CTE wrapper. The tool exposes this directly to the LLM.
findings.fix_hint: Use a real parser (sqlglot is already a small dep). Parse the statement and require the root be one of SelectStatement/PragmaStatement/ExplainStatement and that no DML/DDL nodes appear anywhere in the tree. Alternatively, set the SQLite connection to `PRAGMA query_only = 1` and Postgres to `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` for the duration of `query`.
findings.verifiable_by: Call database(action='query', driver='sqlite', sql='WITH x AS (SELECT 1) DELETE FROM cards WHERE 1=1'); expect rejection.

findings.title: execute mutates without a checkpoint or transaction snapshot
findings.description: execute commits immediately with no checkpoint. The docstring acknowledges this ('not auto-checkpointed because they could span millions of rows; the agent must confirm explicitly') but the safety classifier is opt-in and does not flag database.execute by default.
findings.impact: An LLM-driven UPDATE without WHERE clause silently wipes a column.
findings.fix_hint: Require `confirmed=true` in args for any execute call; without it, return needs_confirmation with the SQL and a row-count preview from a wrapping SELECT (best-effort). The safety pending flow already supports this.
findings.verifiable_by: Call database(action='execute', sql='DELETE FROM cards'); expect needs_confirmation.

findings.title: Postgres/MySQL password passes through args and may be echoed in traces
findings.description: When the LLM calls database(driver='postgres', password='...'), the args dict is logged by the registry's `_normalize_tool_result` and persisted to `traces.jsonl`. The password appears in cleartext in the trace.
findings.evidence:
conn = psycopg.connect(
    host=args.get("host", "localhost"),
    port=int(args.get("port", 5432)),
    user=args.get("user"),
    password=args.get("password"),
    ...
findings.impact: Credential leak via traces. Anyone with read access to the project state directory can recover the DB password.
findings.fix_hint: Redact 'password', 'token', 'key' keys from the args before they hit `evidence`/`stdout`/trace. Or only accept `password_env=<VARNAME>` and read from os.environ.
findings.verifiable_by: Run database connect with password='secret'; grep traces.jsonl for 'secret'; expect no match.

tools.name: backup_sync
tools.signature: backup_sync_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: _backup_restore does not sanitize zip entry paths (zip-slip)
findings.description: For every entry the code does `final_target = dst / entry.filename` then writes the file. zipfile.ZipFile does not normalize `../` or absolute paths in entry names. A crafted backup zip can write to `C:/Windows/...` or `..../etc/important` outside `dst`.
findings.evidence:
for entry in entries:
    if entry.is_dir():
        (dst / entry.filename).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        continue
    final_target = dst / entry.filename
    final_target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ...
    with archive.open(entry, "r") as src_fh, final_target.open("wb") as dst_fh:
        shutil.copyfileobj(src_fh, dst_fh)
findings.impact: Path traversal: a malicious zip can place files anywhere the agent user can write. Since backup_sync zips are created by the agent itself this is mostly self-trust, but if the user restores a zip received elsewhere the breach is total.
findings.fix_hint: Before writing, resolve `final_target` and verify it is contained within `dst.resolve()` (use Path.resolve(strict=False) and check `dst.resolve() in final_target.resolve().parents or final_target.resolve() == dst.resolve()`). Reject any entry where this fails.
findings.verifiable_by: Build a zip containing `..\evil.txt` and call backup_sync(action='restore'); expect rejection with status='failed'.

findings.title: restore does not snapshot the dst tree before overwriting
findings.description: With conflict='overwrite', files in `dst` are silently replaced. There is no checkpoint metadata (unlike `filesystem` mutations which call `_checkpoint_existing_path`). state.rollback cannot undo the restore.
findings.evidence:
elif conflict_policy == "overwrite":
    overwritten.append({"name": entry.filename})
...
with archive.open(entry, "r") as src_fh, final_target.open("wb") as dst_fh:
    shutil.copyfileobj(src_fh, dst_fh)
findings.impact: Restoring a backup with overwrite policy is irreversible.
findings.fix_hint: Before the first overwrite, copy the existing dst tree to a sibling backup directory and register a checkpoint with rollback that restores from that copy.
findings.verifiable_by: restore with overwrite then state.rollback; expect prior content recovered.

tools.name: notification
tools.signature: notification_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: _schedule_notification embeds a quoted PS sub-command into another quoted PS argument
findings.description: display_script = `Add-Type ... [System.Windows.MessageBox]::Show('<text>','<title>')` (single-quoted, _ps_quote applied). Then this display_script is embedded inside `'-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "<display_script>"'` — the outer wrapper is single-quoted but the inner uses double quotes. If `text` or `title` (LLM-controlled) contains `"`, the outer Argument string is broken and PowerShell injection follows. _ps_quote only escapes `'` (single quotes); it does not touch double quotes.
findings.evidence:
display_script = f"Add-Type -AssemblyName PresentationFramework; [System.Windows.MessageBox]::Show('{_ps_quote(text)}','{_ps_quote(title)}')"
ps = f"""
$Action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument '-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "{display_script}"'
$Trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date '{due.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}')
...
findings.impact: PowerShell command injection via notification.toast_schedule/timer_start/reminder_create when text or title contain `"`. The injected payload runs at the scheduled time under the user's account.
findings.fix_hint: Drop the nested quoting entirely: register the Scheduled Task with `New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute powershell.exe -Argument '-NoProfile -File <script.ps1>'` where script.ps1 is a fixed file in the state dir, and pass title/text via $env:GEMMA4_TITLE/$env:GEMMA4_TEXT (set via -Argument parameters or registered task variables). Or store the message in agent state and have the runner read it by id.
findings.verifiable_by: Call notification(action='reminder_create', title='a', text='x";Stop-Computer;"'); inspect the generated Scheduled Task XML and confirm no injected command.

findings.title: _notification_due falls back to now+5min if parsing fails — silent UX bug
findings.description: If `due` is provided as a malformed string (e.g. '15:00' without date) parsing fails and the function silently uses 'now + 5 minutes'. The schedule fires at the wrong time and the LLM/user are not warned.
findings.impact: Wrong-time alarms with no error signal.
findings.fix_hint: If parsing fails, return a validation error from notification_tool BEFORE registering anything. Accept HH:MM by interpreting as today/tomorrow; reject everything else.
findings.verifiable_by: Call notification(action='alarm_create', time='15:00'); expect validation error or correct today-15:00 due.

tools.name: maintenance
tools.signature: maintenance_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: _maintenance_event_logs interpolates `log` arg into the PS FilterHashtable literal
findings.description: `log` arg is embedded inside the PowerShell hashtable literal `@{ LogName='{log}'; ... }` via Python f-string without escaping. A log value containing `'` breaks the literal; a value containing `' ; Stop-Computer ; #` allows arbitrary PS execution.
findings.evidence:
cmd = (
    f"$start = (Get-Date).AddHours(-{hours}); "
    f"$f = @{{ LogName='{log}'; StartTime=$start"
    f"{'' if level is None else f'; Level={int(level)}'}"
    f" }}; "
    f"Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable $f -MaxEvents {limit} -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ..."
)
findings.impact: PowerShell command injection via maintenance(action='event_logs_query', log=...). LLM-controlled.
findings.fix_hint: Use the env-var indirection pattern: set $env:GEMMA4_LOG = log, then PS reads $env:GEMMA4_LOG. Or build the hashtable in a JSON blob via $env and use `ConvertFrom-Json` then cast keys.
findings.verifiable_by: Call maintenance(action='event_logs_query', log="System' ; Write-Output INJECTED ; #"); confirm no injection in stdout.

findings.title: defender_quick_scan blocks the agent thread up to 15 minutes
findings.description: Start-MpScan -ScanType QuickScan runs synchronously; subprocess.run waits up to 900 seconds. The agent is unresponsive during this window and the user cannot cancel via the tool.
findings.evidence:
proc = subprocess.run(
    ["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", "Start-MpScan -ScanType QuickScan"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900,
)
findings.impact: 15-minute blackout. No way to cancel except killing the agent process.
findings.fix_hint: Launch via job_manager.start (already designed for long-running jobs) and return the job_id immediately. The agent polls job_manager.status_of to know completion.
findings.verifiable_by: Call maintenance(action='defender_quick_scan'); expect a job_id and ability to cancel.

findings.title: disk_cleanup_describe returns command_describe=['cleanmgr','/sageset:1'] but says 'we do not run this'
findings.description: The describe action returns cleanmgr command strings and status='needs_user'. The LLM can take the returned `command_describe` array and feed it to terminal() to run anyway. The 'we do not run this automatically' note is a soft contract that the LLM can ignore.
findings.impact: Soft gate around a destructive action. cleanmgr /sagerun:1 deletes selected categories irreversibly.
findings.fix_hint: Return the description as prose only, no executable command array. Or require explicit confirmed=true on a separate maintenance.disk_cleanup_run action.
findings.verifiable_by: Static review.

tools.name: routine
tools.signature: routine_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState, executor: Executor | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: _build_routine_trigger_ps interpolates trigger.at / days_of_week into PowerShell
findings.description: trigger.at (string), trigger.days_of_week (list joined by ','), trigger.interval_minutes (cast to int OK) are f-string-interpolated into PowerShell expressions like `New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At '{at}'`. A trigger.at value containing `'` escapes the string and a longer payload runs PS.
findings.evidence:
if cadence == "daily":
    return f"New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At '{at}'"
if cadence == "weekly":
    raw_days = trigger.get("days_of_week")
    days: list[Any] = raw_days if isinstance(raw_days, list) else ["Monday"]
    days_str = ",".join(str(d) for d in days)
    return f"New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Weekly -DaysOfWeek {days_str} -At '{at}'"
findings.impact: PowerShell command injection via routine(action='create', trigger={'cadence':'daily','at':"08:00' ; Stop-Computer ; #"}). The injection runs at task registration time under the agent's user.
findings.fix_hint: Validate at against a strict regex `^[0-2]\d:[0-5]\d$` (and ISO date for `once`). Validate days_of_week against the literal set {Monday..Sunday}. Refuse anything else.
findings.verifiable_by: Call routine(action='create', trigger={'type':'cron','cadence':'daily','at':"08:00';Write-Host pwn;#"}); expect validation error.

findings.title: routine_tool reaches into state._load() / state._save() throughout
findings.description: Lines 576-580 (and similar in many helpers) use `state._load()` and `state._save(data)` directly, mutating the internal dict and writing back. AgentState has a public API (register_resource, mark_cleaned, checkpoint); the private-API workaround bypasses any concurrency lock or schema validation that the public API enforces. (The recent commit 3f77637 added RLock to JSON stores — these direct reads/writes likely skip that lock unless _load/_save themselves acquire it.)
findings.evidence:
data = state._load()
rec = data.get("resources", {}).get(routine_id)
if rec:
    rec.setdefault("metadata", {})["watcher_id"] = watcher_id
    state._save(data)
findings.impact: Race conditions where two tools modify resources concurrently can lose updates. Schema drift if AgentState changes its internal shape.
findings.fix_hint: Add a public `state.update_resource_metadata(resource_id, patch)` method and refactor all `state._load()/_save()` callers to it. Confirm the RLock guards both read and write inside the helper.
findings.verifiable_by: grep `_load\|_save` outside state.py; expect zero matches after fix.

findings.title: _looks_destructive contains a redundant/buggy boolean chain
findings.description: Line 284 reads `if needle in low or low.find(" " + needle.split()[0]) >= 0 and needle in low`. Python precedence makes this `needle in low or ((low.find(...)>=0) and (needle in low))` which simplifies to just `needle in low`. The intended word-boundary check is duplicated by `boundary_hits` below. The first half does nothing useful and obscures the logic.
findings.impact: Dead code, harder to maintain; behavior is correct only because boundary_hits below covers the real check.
findings.fix_hint: Remove the entire first loop; keep only `boundary_hits = [t for t in _DESTRUCTIVE_COMMAND_TOKENS if re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(t)}\b', command, re.IGNORECASE)]`.
findings.verifiable_by: Diff confirms simplification; unit tests on `_looks_destructive('shutdown /s /t 0')` still return True.

tools.name: smart_home
tools.signature: smart_home_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: _hass_alive returns True even when HA is unreachable
findings.description: The outer `except Exception` block catches connection refused, DNS failure, timeout — and then *unconditionally* tries to `import urllib.error` and returns True. The comment claims '401 still means HA is alive', but the code does not distinguish HTTPError(401) from URLError(ConnectionRefusedError). Every reachability failure registers as alive.
findings.impact: smart_home(action='status') reports `home_assistant=True` even when HA is down. Downstream calls fail with confusing HTTP errors instead of an honest 'not reachable'.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the inner except with: `except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.code in (200, 401, 403)`. For URLError/timeout/other: return False. Remove the `import urllib.error` no-op.
findings.verifiable_by: Stop HA / change GEMMA4_HASS_HOST to a port that does not listen; call smart_home(action='status'); expect home_assistant=False.

findings.title: _hass_call_service rollback only handles binary on/off; brightness/color not snapshotted
findings.description: Rollback step is constructed only for `turn_on`/`turn_off`/`toggle`. A `light.turn_on` with brightness=255 cannot be rolled back to the prior brightness of 50; rollback would just turn it off.
findings.impact: Half-faithful rollback. Acceptable but documented; users may expect color/brightness restoration.
findings.fix_hint: When state.state == 'on' and we're turning off OR changing attributes, snapshot the full state dict and craft a rollback that turns on with the same attributes (brightness, hs_color, color_temp, etc).
findings.verifiable_by: Set a light to brightness 50, call_service turn_on brightness 255, then state.rollback; expect brightness 50 again.

tools.name: network
tools.signature: network_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: _network_dns_set joins addresses into a PowerShell expression without escaping
findings.description: addresses (list of strings) is joined via `",".join(f"'{a}'" for a in addresses)` and embedded into the PowerShell `Set-DnsClientServerAddress ... -ServerAddresses ({addr_list})` literal. If any address contains `'`, the PowerShell argument is broken and additional commands execute.
findings.evidence:
addr_list = ",".join(f"'{a}'" for a in addresses)
cmd = f"Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceAlias '{_ps_quote(adapter)}' -ServerAddresses ({addr_list})"
findings.impact: PowerShell command injection via network(action='dns_set', addresses=["8.8.8.8'; Stop-Computer; #"]).
findings.fix_hint: Validate each address against `^\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}$` (IPv4) or `^[0-9a-fA-F:]+$` (IPv6) before embedding. Anything else: reject. Or pass addresses via $env:GEMMA4_DNS_ADDRS and let PS split.
findings.verifiable_by: Call network(action='dns_set', adapter='Wi-Fi', addresses=["8.8.8.8' ; pwn ; '"]); expect rejection.

findings.title: _network_connections passes `state` arg straight into Get-NetTCPConnection -State
findings.description: `state_filter` (LLM-controlled) is interpolated into `-State {state_filter}` without quoting. PowerShell parses it as a parameter argument; values that contain `; cmd` would parse as additional pipeline elements.
findings.evidence:
state_filter = str(args.get("state") or "Established").strip()
proc = subprocess.run(
    ["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", f"Get-NetTCPConnection -State {state_filter} ..."],
    ...
findings.impact: Lower-likelihood PS injection: PS treats `-State` as expecting an enum value; unknown enum members error out. But `Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established ; Stop-Computer ; #` is syntactically valid PowerShell.
findings.fix_hint: Validate against the documented enum: {Closed, CloseWait, Closing, DeleteTcb, Established, FinWait1, FinWait2, LastAck, Listen, SynReceived, SynSent, TimeWait}. Reject anything else.
findings.verifiable_by: Call network(action='connections', state='Established;pwn'); expect rejection.

tools.name: data_analysis
tools.signature: data_analysis_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: csv_query passes user string to pandas .query() without engine restriction
findings.description: pandas .query() uses numexpr if available, otherwise falls back to python's `eval` (with engine='python'). Even with numexpr the parser supports `@` to reference Python locals and backticked column names; with python engine, backtick-wrapped expressions can call arbitrary names in the local namespace. Pandas docs explicitly warn about this for untrusted input.
findings.evidence: result = df.query(query)
findings.impact: Potential RCE depending on numexpr presence; at minimum the LLM can introspect Python locals. Lower risk than `eval` directly but the API is not designed for adversarial input.
findings.fix_hint: Force `engine='numexpr'` if available and reject queries containing `@` or backticks. Or run the query in a multiprocessing worker with a strict resource limit. Or replace with a small AST-validated DSL.
findings.verifiable_by: Call data_analysis(action='csv_query', query='@__import__("os").system("echo x")') ; expect rejection or numexpr ParserError.

tools.name: developer
tools.signature: developer_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: stop_dev_server kills the stored PID without checking it is still owned by the dev server
findings.description: Windows recycles PIDs. The dev server may have exited and a new process (e.g. Discord) may now hold the same PID. taskkill /F /PID kills that unrelated process tree.
findings.impact: Risk of killing the wrong process when restarting agent or after long uptime.
findings.fix_hint: Before taskkill, verify `Get-Process -Id <pid>` returns the same exe name as `metadata.cmd[0]`. If not, refuse and report the mismatch.
findings.verifiable_by: Manually overwrite a recorded dev_server pid in state to a PID owned by an unrelated process; expect refusal.

findings.title: start_dev_server uses Popen but does not detach from agent process group
findings.description: On Windows, without DETACHED_PROCESS or CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, the child remains in the agent's job. When the agent exits the dev server can be killed by the OS. CREATE_NO_WINDOW alone hides the console but does not detach.
findings.evidence:
creationflags = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW if os.name == "nt" else 0
proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=str(root), stdout=log_file, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, creationflags=creationflags)
findings.impact: Dev server dies when the agent stops; user must re-launch.
findings.fix_hint: Add `subprocess.CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | subprocess.DETACHED_PROCESS` (with appropriate stdout redirection) so the dev server survives agent shutdown.
findings.verifiable_by: Start dev server, kill agent, check the dev server PID is still alive.

tools.signature: browser_real_tool(args: dict[str, Any], state: AgentState, captures_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]

findings.title: browser_real(action='evaluate') accepts arbitrary JavaScript from the LLM
findings.description: The `evaluate` action runs `page.evaluate(script)` with the LLM-supplied script string. On a CDP-attached visible browser, the script runs in the page context with the user's cookies/session, which means it can exfiltrate session tokens, send messages on Slack/Gmail, etc.
findings.impact: Full take-over surface of the attached browser. Sensitive on a visible session.
findings.fix_hint: Gate evaluate behind a confirmation when session is CDP (visible/user profile). For headless agent-owned sessions keep it open. Document the risk in the schema description.
findings.verifiable_by: Call browser_real(action='evaluate', script='document.cookie') on a CDP session; expect needs_confirmation.

findings.title: _BROWSER_SESSIONS is module-global and not lifecycle-managed by AgentState
findings.description: Module-global dict; on process restart the sessions are lost but state.json still references them. Reconnecting requires re-issuing attach_visible. The `resource` registered in state is orphaned.
findings.evidence:
_PW: Any | None = None
_BROWSER_SESSIONS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
findings.impact: Stale resources accumulate in state across restarts; cleanup_plan tries to close sessions that no longer exist.
findings.fix_hint: On startup, mark any browser_real resource with metadata.process_uptime != current as stale and prune. Or move session metadata to state and lazy-reconnect.
findings.verifiable_by: Start agent, attach_visible, restart agent, state(action='resources'); expect the stale session pruned.

findings.title: _get_browser_session ignores headless flag after first call
findings.description: Once a session exists, the function returns it as-is regardless of the requested `headless`. A second call to open(headless=False) silently uses the existing headless=True session.
findings.impact: Schema contract drift; user expects a visible browser and gets headless.
findings.fix_hint: If session.headless != requested headless, return _err('session already open with different headless; close first', status='needs_user').
findings.verifiable_by: Call open(headless=True), then open(headless=False); expect the second to refuse.

findings.title: wait_for_download returns needs_implementation for CDP sessions
findings.description: Documented in the docstring of `_browser_wait_for_download`. Honest gap, but the user must know that attach_visible + click that triggers a download cannot be awaited via this tool path.
findings.impact: Workflow gap. Not a defect, but the schema description says 'wait_for_download requires the click that triggers the download to happen inside the same call chain' which is not explicit about CDP limitation.
findings.fix_hint: Update the schema description for browser_real to call out the CDP limitation. Long-term: add a raw CDP Browser.downloadProgress listener path.
findings.verifiable_by: Schema review.

findings.title: AppResolver.open swallows os.startfile errors silently
findings.description: os.startfile raises OSError on missing files / failed protocol handlers. There is no try/except; the registry's broad except surfaces a generic 'OSError:' to the LLM. The verifier cannot tell whether the launch was attempted or failed.

cross_cutting.title: Recurring pattern: f-string interpolation of LLM-controlled args into PowerShell scripts
cross_cutting.description: Multiple tools build PowerShell -Command strings by f-string interpolation of LLM-controlled arguments. _ps_quote only doubles single quotes; it does NOT escape double quotes, backticks, $ signs, or any character that breaks PowerShell parsing when the value is embedded outside a single-quoted literal. There is no consistent helper for 'escape this for the position where it will be used'. The codebase already shows the correct pattern (env-var indirection: set $env:GEMMA4_X=value, then PS reads $env:GEMMA4_X) in several places — `window_control`, `_env_ps`, `_file_hash`, `_authenticode_signature`, `_scanner_scan`. Apply uniformly.
cross_cutting.fix_hint: Adopt the env-var indirection pattern everywhere: never f-string LLM data into PS scripts. If the value MUST appear in a script literal (e.g. inside a hashtable key), validate against a strict regex first (e.g. `^[A-Za-z0-9_\-:.]+$` for log names, `^\d{2}:\d{2}$` for times, IP regex for addresses). Add a single helper `_ps_safe_literal(value, regex)` that returns the value or raises.

cross_cutting.title: Destructive tools execute without confirmation by default
cross_cutting.description: ToolRegistry.safety_enabled defaults to False. The classify_tool_call gate is the only mechanism that converts destructive intents into needs_confirmation. By default, shutdown/restart, terminal arbitrary commands, package install/uninstall, database execute, backup_sync restore with overwrite, and filesystem delete all execute immediately on LLM intent. The form_filler tool shows the correct pattern: a hard `confirmed=true` gate that produces a screenshot and creates a pending confirmation regardless of registry settings.
cross_cutting.fix_hint: 1) Switch ToolRegistry default to safety_enabled=True. 2) For each tool in the affected list, add an unconditional needs_confirmation flow (not just behind safety_enabled). 3) The confirmation should include a short summary of what will happen and the inverse-action availability.

cross_cutting.title: Tools mutate AgentState through private _load()/_save() methods
cross_cutting.description: Multiple call sites in domain_tools.py use `state._load()` then mutate the returned dict in place and call `state._save(data)`. This bypasses the public API and any locking the AgentState class enforces. The repo's recent fix (commit 3f77637) added RLock to JSON stores; whether _load/_save themselves acquire the lock around the load-modify-save pattern is unclear without reading state.py — but even if they do per-call, the user's modifications between calls are unprotected.
cross_cutting.fix_hint: Add a public `state.update_resource(resource_id, *, metadata_patch=None, cleanup_args_patch=None)` and refactor every call site. The wrapper should acquire the RLock, read, merge, save atomically.

cross_cutting.title: Many tools call json.loads(proc.stdout) without try/except
cross_cutting.description: Even though `_powershell_json` (domain_tools.py:7205) and `_json_or_text` (ops_tools.py:1102) helpers exist that handle this correctly, several call sites in tools.py and a few in domain_tools.py still call `json.loads(proc.stdout)` directly. When PowerShell prints a warning before the JSON, the parse fails and the registry surfaces a generic JSONDecodeError to the LLM.
cross_cutting.fix_hint: Replace direct json.loads(stdout) with _json_or_text or _powershell_json (consolidate to a single helper in a new gemma4_agent/_ps.py). Add a fallback path that returns _err with stdout truncated when JSON fails.

cross_cutting.title: taskkill /F /PID without verifying process identity
cross_cutting.description: Both _developer_stop_dev_server and _job_manager_cancel call `taskkill /F /PID <pid> /T` on a PID stored at job-start time. Windows recycles PIDs; the same PID may belong to an unrelated process after the recorded one exits. There is no verification that the PID still corresponds to the recorded exe name.
cross_cutting.fix_hint: Before taskkill, run `Get-Process -Id <pid>` and check that ProcessName starts with the recorded cmd[0] basename. If not, refuse and report 'pid_recycled'.

cross_cutting.title: Credentials passed through args are logged to traces
cross_cutting.description: Tools accept password/token in their args dict; `_normalize_tool_result` and the agent's tracing layer write the full args to traces.jsonl. database.password, smart_home.token, email tokens via env (OK) — but database/smart_home accept inline credentials and persist them.
cross_cutting.fix_hint: Add a registry-level redaction pass for keys named 'password', 'token', 'key', 'secret' before persisting traces. Or accept only `password_env=<VARNAME>` and read from os.environ inside the tool.

cross_cutting.title: GUI screenshot uses VirtualScreen; OCR coords need explicit screen translation
cross_cutting.description: Screenshot captures VirtualScreen across monitors. click_text translates with shot.left/top correctly, but the OCR result fields (center_x, center_y) are image-local, not screen-local. The LLM can mis-click if it extracts those values directly.
cross_cutting.fix_hint: Add `screen_x`/`screen_y` to OCR match outputs (pre-translated) and document image_local vs screen_local in the schema.

cross_cutting.title: state.rollback executes every stored rollback step without further gating
cross_cutting.description: state(action='rollback') iterates the stored rollback steps and dispatches them via the registry's execute. Some rollback steps are themselves destructive (e.g. filesystem.delete to undo a copy). The form is correct but the LLM can chain it implicitly. Not a defect, but worth noting in the schema description.
cross_cutting.fix_hint: Document in state's schema that rollback executes steps verbatim. Consider returning rollback_plan first by default and requiring an explicit second call to apply.
